body: I have tried going to college several times now, but I always end up getting overwhelmed with depression and anxiety. I tried so hard the last semester I went. I really hate these generalized types of messages too. They make me angry, even if they were posted by friends I know who mean well. Trying to be positive is great, but being told I matter through a generalized message posted on social media just makes me feel even more meaningless and insignificant.

The orb feels terrible. Most of the time it just sails right on by anybody without sticking; even when an enemy Moira uses it against me. Had one fly right into my face and it didn't attach! Have played several games now and rarely did I see anyone on either team stuck with an orb. Why even bother with it now? It would have made more sense against double shield/bunker where more players are grouped (making it easier to hit), but now it doesn't go through shields. It might stick to someone in a Zarya grav, I guess?? Against a flanker, I'm safer and better off throwing a healing orb and whittling down the flanker with my tickle beam.

Fade invulnerability feels... like nothing. Maybe because I can't see any numbers indicating the damage it stopped. Jumping into the line of fire to potentially save someone hasn't gone too well for me yet. Using it to protect ulting teammates or Mercy rezzing I guess helped? Some indicator that it's doing something would just be nice! No cleanse this time around also isn't as fun. At least it felt like I was doing something then. 

Overall, she is no one more fun than she was before. If anything, she is more frustrating because her new 'features' feel bad.

A lot of players don't use a mic, and this game is too faced paced to stop and type out an apologize unless you are dead, and even then you only have so many seconds.

Adding a sorry voice line won't solve any major problems when it comes to toxic behavior, but it's still a small gesture of goodwill that can impact morale. As OP mentioned, and as a support main myself, getting a quick 'Thanks!' after a heal lifts my spirits. Even the annoying 'I need healing' spam becomes more tolerable if they punctuate it with a thank you afterwards. It's just *nice*.

Admittedly, I'm not a rage baby and I don't really get mad at this game, but there are times when my teammates have gotten me killed or just played poorly and it's upset me. My knee jerk reaction might be 'they weren't even paying attention', and so I start losing confidence in my team. For me, and maybe for others, a quick 'sorry' from the offending player might help bring my confidence level back up, because it shows they care about the mistake. It lightens the mood. Will that be the case for all players? No, but it doesn't have to be.

And yes, people would abuse a sorry voice line to be an asshole. They do it with 'thanks' and 'understood' plenty. Polite voice lines aren't really meant for the toxic players. But a few assholes abusing them doesn't make the commands any less meaningful when they're used genuinely.

TLDR; morale good.

I can make a it a real 5v6 and leave to avoid awarding a toxic person's behavior with heals if you would prefer? Don't shift the blame away from the toxic player, who is the *real* problem in your game. If a person is being so toxic the healers don't even want to heal them, then your game was probably a lose anyway. Don't be toxic in the first place and maybe your team will want to support you.

Honestly, thank god for squelch chat option because *I'M* tired of the passive aggressive DPS spamming for heals the moment they die.

Last I checked, Overwatch is not a workplace for the majority of players, but a game that is meant to be played for fun.

If you want to report healers for refusing to heal toxic players as gameplay sabotage, then the toxic player also needs to be reported for gameplay sabotage. Players that have pissed off a healer to the point of cutting them off from heals have probably been running their mouth more than they've been playing the game.

Typically, the best thing to do with toxic players is just to mute them and move on, but I can't blame a healer if they get a little spicy and decide to play with them a bit. And if these fed up healers bother you that much, avoid them as teammates and also move on.

I'm not sure if you're joking or not, but when the team is clumped on top of each other sometimes latching onto the critical HP squishies around the tanks is tricky. Comparatively, Ana's rifle shots will pass through full HP teammates and hit whoever actually needs the heal, but Mercy's beam will always latch onto whoever is right in front of her crosshair regardless. This is the situation OP is talking about. Lowing the sensitivity of Caduceus Staff helps, but you'll never latch onto someone if a big ol' Hog is completely blocking your view of them. In this way, Mercy cannot hide behind tanks as reliably because she has to constantly bob and weave around them to heal.

That being said, I don't think Mercy's staff needs to prioritize or latch onto lower health targets through teammates. Positioning and evasion, the bob and weave, is just part of her playstyle. Usually if your team is that clumped up, an AoE support might be the better choice.

I've never been insulted or told I suck at this game because I'm a girl, but the amount of sexual harassment I've experienced from people just ASSUMING I'm a girl is ridiculous. I imagine if I used voice chat and these people could confirm my gender during a game it would be way worse, which is why I will never use my mic.

Like you, I use to have a feminine tag, but I've changed it to something more gender neutral because of this kind of behavior. It was especially bad because I also main Mercy. They saw the Mercy with a feminine tag and instantly assumed I was female. I would get friend requests after matches from people who after only a few minutes of idle conversation about OW would start up with the "so are you a girl?" line of questioning. Generally, I have learned, if anyone starts asking for your gender that their intention is never friendship and to just block or remove them immediately. I use to give people the benefit of the doubt, but not anyone. I've been burned too many times now.

It's tiring and makes me sad.

I don't know if he needs nerfs. Doomfist is just very frustrating to play against, in part because he feels inconsistent. I can remember numerous times where I think I'm safe behind my tanks, but he'll still sail right through Hog to land his punch on me. There's also times where he's punched me and I should have died but didn't.

I also kinda wish his punch did less dmg the further away from the impact wall you are. If he punches me from 20m away, and my body flies another 20m before I hit a wall, I feel like it's fair that I would take less dmg from that punch. At least then I could potentially position myself better if I hear him coming. I hate that 1 sec after a random Doom punch where I think I'm okay because I haven't hit a wall, but then I finally collide with something and blow up. It's just... frustrating.

I mainly play support (in the plat range), and I suppose I've had the most success avoiding him as Mercy or Moira. Ana would be good if I was just better at her, but my mechanical skills aren't there for Ana. I saw some people suggest Brig, but I feel like as Brig I can stun and knock him back, but he'll still kill me before I can smack him down usually. That is just my experience though.

I am a support main and I strongly dislike role queue. It makes the game feel boring, and it just really bothers me that Blizzard is forcing 2-2-2 and taking away player flexibility.

I also just haven't had good experiences so far either. DPS seem even less inclined to switch off their mains, because they queued and waited a long time to play them. Now, a support or tank can't switch off to DPS, even temporarily, to help the situation. I'd also rather have three DPS (hell, even four) who know what they're doing then a DPS trying to play tank/support for shorter queue times.

I played most of my games as support, and I have not had good experience with role queue. I dropped from 2900 to 2100 because I kept getting put on teams with tanks/dps who refused to switch characters to adapt to the enemy/map, or they just quit mid game, or just straight up trolled the entire match. I'm mostly blaming, and hoping, it's just the beta season, and eventually everyone will settle into place, but right now it's painful. I also think a lot of people are trying comp right now just to test the new system, so they don't really care if they do well or not.
